The House Ag GOP bill claims to support farmers but hides the real cost—slashing $28B from SNAP to fund a 56% spike in crop subsidies. Reference price hikes for soybeans (19%), cotton (140%), and peanuts (69%) skew heavily toward Southern crops, leaving Midwest growers with scraps.

Real reform prioritizes all farmers without robbing food security programs.

Cut the bloat, fund direct solutions, and let Kansas farmers—not federal middlemen—lead stewardship.
